title: Regional residency locks, zone-preference packing, and safe-drain policy for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Gomez
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Dedicated in multi-AZ and multi-region setups need deterministic throughput guarantees and strict data residency controls while still getting the operational benefits of autoscaling and graceful failover. Current placement policies are coarse: they either favor region-only placement or strict zone affinity that can cause capacity fragmentation and breach throughput SLAs during drains and failovers.

This ticket proposes three coordinated features: (1) regional residency locks (a soft residency contract that pins traffic to a region but allows controlled, auditable overflow under policy), (2) zone-preference packing (pack GPUs into small coherent sets to reduce cross-zone data movement and make gradual drains efficient), and (3) a safe-drain protocol that reserves transient capacity and enforces throughput guarantees during node/zone maintenance or emergency failover.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Residency lock API: customers can create/update/delete residency locks that specify region, allowed overflow regions, max overflow fraction, and TTL; operations are audited and visible in Console.
2) Zone-preference packing: serving runtime will expose a placement hint to the orchestrator enabling grouping of a customer's instances into 'packs' of size N (configurable). Packs should not span more than M zones unless explicitly allowed.
3) Safe-drain protocol: when a zone is drained, orchestrator allocates reserve tokens to maintain configured throughput percent (e.g., 90%) for up to X minutes while moving traffic, and falls back to overflow policy when reserve is depleted.
4) End-to-end tests and canary: automated tests that simulate zone drain under mixed workloads must pass, and canary rollout demonstrating no >10% throughput regression for a set of sampled customers.
5) Console UI hooks for creating residency locks and viewing active drains and audit trails.
6) Audit logs and metrics emitted for every policy decision (placement override, pack move, reserve token consumption).
design_decisions:
- Use a soft residency lock rather than immutable zoning to balance availability and data-sovereignty requirements. Locks have a TTL and an explicit overflow policy to avoid silent cross-region routing.
- Implement 'packs' as first-class placement units in the orchestrator: packs are assigned to a zone and treated atomically during drains. Pack size default is 8 GPUs, tunable per-customer.
- Safe-drain leverages a token-bucket style reserve: each pack has a small reserve allocation tracked in the placement controller; when drained, the controller reroutes new requests to overflow targets but uses reserve tokens to keep in-flight sessions on original pack until completion or reserve exhaustion.
- Placement policy expressed as a declarative schema (residency_lock object) validated by API server and enforced by placement controller; console exposes legacy compatibility mode for customers that already manage strict zone affinity.
- Policy enforcement will be eventual-consistent but observable: decisions are logged and reconciled by a background verifier with exponential backoff to avoid flapping.
- For throughput guarantees, prioritize existing sticky connections and use a graceful handoff with KV cache snapshotting to reduce quality degradation during pack reassignment.
implementation_notes:
- API changes: add /v1/dedicated/residency_locks endpoints; RBAC checks required.
- Orchestrator: extend pack metadata, add pack-to-zone binding state and drain lifecycle states (DRAINING, DRAIN_HANDOFF, DRAIN_COMPLETED).
- Serving runtime: expose pack-id and allow KV cache snapshot/restore hooks.
- Autoscaler: aware of pack boundaries; scale activities move whole packs where possible.
- Telemetry: new metrics: residency_lock.evaluations, pack.moves, drain.reserve_tokens.{used,remaining}, overflow.routed_requests.
- Default config: max overflow fraction = 10%, pack size = 8, reserve duration = 600s.
- Backwards compatibility: customers without residency locks continue to use the current placement logic.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flags: residency-locks, pack-placement, safe-drain in backend and console.
2) Internal dogfood: enable for infra teams in region-us-west-2, run synthetic traffic with mixed seq-lens.
3) Canary customers: opt-in customers with low-risk workloads. Monitor throughput, latency p99, and error rate.
4) Gradual enablement: open to >20% of dedicated capacity after 2 weeks of stable canary.
5) Full release: 8 weeks after canary if no regression >10% in throughput or increased error rate.
6) Post-release: 30-day monitoring window with automatic rollback triggers tied to SLAs.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for API schema and validation rules.
- Integration tests simulating zone drain with: short text-generation chat sessions, long-running streaming sessions, and KV-cache dependent reuse.
- Chaos tests: kill a zone and measure reserve token consumption, reassign packs, watch routing decisions.
- Performance tests: measure packing effect on tail latency and throughput for co-located packs vs spread placement.
- Security tests: RBAC and KMS interactions for audit logs.
- E2E canary plan: traffic shadowing for 48 hours, then progressive traffic shift.
